Carpenter Contractor Trust launches new website to showcase union workforce resources
S. M. Holmes
The Carpenter Contractor Trust launched a redesigned website at cctmarketing.org, offering contractors, developers, and policymakers a centralized resource to explore the value of the union carpenter workforce across the Eastern Atlantic States, according to an Aug. 26 announcement.
The new site consolidates CCT's expanding library of resources into one platform. Visitors can browse a collection of one-pagers on topics such as apprenticeship programs and project labor agreements, take virtual tours of nine training centers across the Mid-Atlantic States—useful for prospective apprentices—and watch original video features including the Contractor Spotlight series. The site also hosts Labor Lounge, CCT’s monthly podcast co-hosted by executive director Cyndie Williams and Anthony Abrantes, assistant executive secretary-treasurer for the Eastern Atlantic State Regional Council of Carpenters.
“This site is built to make it easy for anyone to see the full scope of what union carpenters and their contractor partners deliver,” Williams said. “Whether someone is looking for a one-pager to bring into a meeting or an episode of the Labor Lounge to listen to on a job site, we wanted all of it in one place.”
The redesigned platform connects visitors with CCT’s network of advocacy websites dedicated to advancing union construction in specific areas: EAS Carpenters (the home page for the Eastern Atlantic States Regional Council), Find a Union Contractor (a directory linking developers with signatory contractors), What Is a PLA (an educational resource on project labor agreements), EAS Data Centers (focused on data center construction), Responsible Wind Energy (highlighting wind energy projects), and Separations Act (tracking Pennsylvania's public construction bidding law). “Each of these sites tells a different piece of the story, but they all point back to the same mission,” Williams said. “Bringing them together on our own homepage makes that connection clear for anyone who visits.”
CCT represents partnerships between union carpenters and signatory contractors throughout six states—New Jersey, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Delaware, West Virginia, Virginia—and Washington D.C., connecting more than 42,000 skilled workers with regional infrastructure projects. The new website was developed by Whitmer Consulting and MediaCutlet.
The New Jersey Business and Industry Association serves as the nation's largest statewide employer association representing private-sector employers throughout New Jersey; it facilitates partnerships among businesses, government entities, and academic institutions while offering advocacy services designed to advance competitive excellence among its members, according to its official website.
